gaps: No Japanese cuisine or slow-braise project on the list — just one Asian-American dish.
No Chinese or Sichuan cuisine at all; the wok is underused for its natural home.
No Korean cuisine despite owning a carbon steel wok and feeding a crowd regularly.
Indian cooking is only South Indian; North Indian cuisine (paneer, tandoori flavors) is absent.
Fish and seafood are entirely missing as a protein.
Tofu appears nowhere as a deliberate weeknight protein with real technique behind it.
Ottolenghi-style vegetable-forward Middle Eastern cooking is listed as a cuisine tag but only one dish exists, and it is a stew — no roasted or composed vegetable mains.
Weekend projects are thin — only one dish (Birria Tacos) requires real commitment.

ideas.title: Kakuni (Japanese Braised Pork Belly)
ideas.why: Opens up Japanese cuisine entirely and fills the weekend-project / long-braise gap — the Big Green Egg or Dutch oven makes this sing.

ideas.title: Vegan Mapo Tofu
ideas.why: Introduces Sichuan cuisine and puts the carbon steel wok to work on a numbing-spicy weeknight dish the whole family — including the vegetarian — can eat as-written.

ideas.title: Easy Japchae (Korean Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)
ideas.why: Fills the Korean gap with a crowd-pleasing noodle dish that scales to six easily; meat is optional so the vegetarian adult is covered with a single omission.

ideas.title: Paneer Tikka Masala
ideas.why: Expands Indian cooking beyond South Indian kanji into North Indian tandoori tradition; paneer is a new protein and the Ooni or cast iron delivers the char the marinade deserves.

ideas.title: Roasted Cauliflower & Burnt Aubergine with Tomato Salsa
ideas.why: Adds a composed, technique-driven vegetable main — charring aubergine directly on the gas flame is a new skill — and deepens the Middle Eastern cuisine slot beyond stewing.

ideas.title: Crispy Sesame Baked Tofu & Shiitake Mushrooms
ideas.why: Closes the tofu-as-intentional-protein gap with a sheet-pan technique (cornstarch + panko crust) that produces fried-level crispiness; fast weeknight meatless meal the kids will actually eat.
